security_spec.violation_condition: On RV32 systems with the Sspmpen extension and more than 32 SPMP entries, the kernel context-switches SPMP entries by writing spmpen and spmpenh as separate CSR instructions without disabling supervisor interrupts (sstatus.SIE). An interrupt delivered between these two writes leaves the hart with a partially updated spmpen mask where some entries from the outgoing task remain active alongside entries from the incoming task, violating inter-task memory isolation.
security_spec.summary: Non-atomic spmpen/spmpenh update on RV32 during SPMP context switch creates a window where a U-mode task can access another task's memory if an interrupt fires between the two CSR writes

findings.finding: The Linux kernel (this tree) does not implement the RISC-V Sspmp (Supervisor-level Physical Memory Protection) extension. No spmpen/spmpenh CSR writes, SPMP entry context-switch logic, or SPMP configuration code exists anywhere in arch/riscv or the broader kernel. The vulnerability condition described in the spec — an interrupt window between spmpen and spmpenh writes on RV32 with >32 entries — cannot be triggered because the SPMP context-switch path simply does not exist.
